column7: The paradigm of the didactic model has not always been the norm. The model and method used in Jesus’ age was the *apprentice model.* This model of learning emphasizes knowledge being more ‘caught than taught’ and focuses more on the relationship between student and teacher, than student and curriculum.
column8: The lecture-based model has not always been the norm. The model and method used in Jesus’ time was *the apprenticeship model.* This learning model emphasizes that knowledge is more “caught than taught,” and it focuses more on the relationship between student and teacher than on the relationship between student and curriculum.

column6: The original paragraph refers to the 'didactic model,' which implies a broader educational approach, while the back-translated paragraph specifies the 'lecture-based model,' which narrows the focus to a specific teaching method. column7: The didactic model gradually became the default method over about a millennium, from the first medieval universities of Europe in the 11<sup>th</sup> - 13<sup>th</sup> centuries, the invention of the printing press in the 15<sup>th</sup> century, the enlightenment of the 17<sup>th</sup> & 18<sup>th</sup> century, and the impact of industrial revolution on information and education in the 19<sup>th</sup> & 20<sup>th</sup> centuries.
